column3: The Hebrew leaves the servants’ master unnamed; BSB supplies Ben-hadad.
The Hebrew leaves both the king and Ahab unnamed and says “the chariot”; BSB supplies both designations and uses “his chariot.”
The Hebrew leaves both speakers unnamed and says “streets”; BSB supplies Ben-hadad and Ahab and uses “marketplaces.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and says the lion struck the man; BSB supplies “the prophet” and says that it killed him.
The Hebrew leaves the finder unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet.”
The Hebrew calls the man brought over “a man”; BSB uses “a captive.”
The Hebrew says “he was not there”; BSB supplies “the man” and uses “disappeared.”
The Hebrew leaves the man removing the bandage unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet.”
The Hebrew leaves both speaker and addressee unnamed; BSB supplies “the prophet” and “the king.”
The Hebrew separately says he went to his house and came to Samaria; BSB combines this as going home to Samaria.
